messages.subject: Random effect logistic model
parts:
Hi there, 

I am trying to fit a random effect mix model using INLA, having previously attempted to fit using "glmer" under the frequentist approach. This failed to converge due to large number of random effects in my data. 

The data comes from a case-control type study (1 = case, 0 = control), and a list of risk factors (x1, x2, x3 ...) were calculated for each samples. All variables were categorised into groups, and the data looks as follows: 

res    age            breed   x1  x2  location
0      1 (0-1 yrs)    beef     1    1     A1
0      2 (1-2 yrs)    dairy    1    2     A1
1      1                  beef     1    2     B2
0      1                  beef     2    1     C1
1      3 (>3 yrs)    dairy     3    3     B1
1      2                 beef      1    1     A1
0      3                 beef      2    1     B4
...     ...                ...          ..    ..    ..

There are around 20,000 data points with 9000 distinct locations. The INLA procedure I used is:

formula <- res ~ age + breed + x1 + x2 + x3 + f(location, model = "iid")
model <- inla(formula, data = data, family = "binomial", Ntrials = 1, control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE))


Results from standard logistic regression (excluding random effect) offers similar parameter estimates between "glm" and INLA, however when random effect is included in the model structure as above, parameter estimates (in the logit scale) increased by more than 2 times. This means that when interpreting the odds ratio, it increases exponentially (i.e. exp(parameter estimate)), which does not seems to make sense having an odds ratio of 40...

My question: is the INLA model specification appropriate for this type of analysis? and if so, how do I interpret the results in terms of odds ratios between different risk groups? Also can I use the computed DIC as a model selection criteria between different variable combinations?

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effect logistic model
parts:
I think the problem is that the data aren't informative enough. You
only have slightly more than 2 observations per location, so you don't
have a lot of data to estimate any of the levels of the random effect
(each observation can only be 0 or 1, so you have a small number of
possible values available). The hyper-parameter is thus also poorly
estimated. You thus either need more structure on the location level
(a spatial model? location-level covariates? Group location into
region?), or you should remove it because it's never going to be
informative.

Bob

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effect logistic model
parts:
Hi Bob,

Thanks for your reply, the idea of using random effect is to account for over-dispersion and independence issue in the data, because we suspect that samples from the same location are not entirely independent from each other. Hence model assumptions under standard logistic would be violated.

You are right in that there are large number of levels in the random effect which only contain 1 or 2 observations, but some levels having as many as 40 observations. If i have a list of other location-level variables (such as location type, size of farm etc), will this improve the estimation? Bare in mind that each sample from the same location would have the same location-level variable also.

Grouping into regions may increase the size in each random effect, but the independence issue would still be unresolved right?

Thanks again for your time and help on this.

Cheers

Siben

Hi Havard,

I was trying to implement the new feature of "waic" and "correct.factor", however, was given the following error message: 

"Error in inla.check.control(control.compute, data) : 
  Name `waic' in control-argument `control.compute', is void."

"Error in inla.check.control(control.inla, data) : 
  Name `correct.factor' in control-argument `control.inla', is void."

Maybe I was using the wrong version of the package? Is this feature only available in the testing package? 

The code i used to fit the random effect logistic model is below, just in case that I miss specified something.
formula <- res ~ age + breed + x1 + x2 + x3 + f(location, model = "iid")

model <- inla(formula, data = data, family = "binomial", Ntrials = 1, control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, waic=TRUE), 
              control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=0, prec.intercept = 0.0001), control.family=list(link="logit"), control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE)),
              control.inla=list(correct = TRUE, correct.factor=1))

 Thanks

S
